english.title: Subject of debt relief order under Insolvency Act 1986 dispose of property obtained on credit card not paid for
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a person in respect of whom a debt relief order had been made on **(..SPECIFY DATE OF ORDER..), during the relevant period as defined in section 251R(3) of the Insolvency Act 1986, disposed of property, namely **(..SPECIFY PROPERTY..), which you had obtained on credit card, and at the time of disposal, had not paid for
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 251R(1), 251T(3) and 430 of, and Schedule 10 to, the Insolvency Act 1986.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
subject of a debt relief order under the Act
disposed of property obtained on credit card
not paid for at time of disposal

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) 'Relevant period' means the period between-
(a) the start of the period of two years ending with the application date; and (b) the determination date
(ii) A person is not guilty of an offence under this subsection if the disposal was in the ordinary course of business carried on by the debtor at the time of the disposal - section 251R(4)
(iii) In determining for the purposes of subsection (4) whether any property is disposed of in the ordinary course of a business carried on by the debtor, regard may be had, in particular, to the price paid for the property - section 251R(5)
(iv) A person is not guilty of an offence under this subsection if he proves that, in respect of the conduct constituting the offence, he had no intent to defraud or to conceal the state of his affairs - section 251R(6)
(v) In this section references to disposing of property include pawning or pledging it - section 251R(7)
(vi) It is immaterial for the purposes of this section whether or not the debt relief order is revoked after the conduct constituting an offence takes place (but no offence is committed by virtue of conduct occurring after the order is revoked)
(vii) This offence was Inserted by section 108(1) of and Schedule 17 to the Tribunals, Courts and Enforcement Act 2007.

other.penalty:
Summary: Twelve months and / or a five not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Seven years and / or a fine.

Note: In relation to offences committed before the commencement of section 154(1) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 (limit on magistrates' court powers to impose imprisonment), the reference to "twelve months" is to be read as a reference to "six months".

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
